title: Move a repository between hosts without losing a branch
summary: A clone brings one branch; a mirror brings every ref. Migrate a repository to a new server, keep an automated backup mirror in sync, and verify nothing was left behind.
mental_model: A normal clone is a working copy: one checked-out branch, remote-tracking refs, no tags you did not fetch. A mirror is a copy of the ref namespace itself — every branch, tag and note, laid out exactly as the server has them.

setup.run: sh -c 'git notes add -m "reviewed by the platform team" HEAD'

steps.title: See everything the old server holds
steps.why: Three branches, two tags and a notes ref. A migration that moves only `main` is the commonest way to quietly lose a release branch — so start by counting what must arrive.
steps.expect: Six refs in total: three branches, two tags, one notes ref.

verify.label: the source server has six refs to migrate

steps.title: Watch a normal clone leave things behind
steps.why: A plain clone gives you one checked-out branch and remote-tracking copies of the others. Tags come along, but notes do not — and pushing this clone somewhere else would publish only what it happens to have locally.
steps.expect: One local branch and no notes ref.

verify.label: a normal clone did not bring the notes
verify.hint: notes need their own refspec — a mirror takes them automatically

steps.title: Take a mirror instead
steps.why: `--mirror` implies `--bare` and copies the ref namespace verbatim: every branch as a local branch, every tag, every note. It is the correct starting point for a migration or a backup.
steps.expect: All six refs, laid out exactly as on the server.

verify.label: …including the notes a normal clone skipped

steps.title: Push the mirror to the new host
steps.why: `push --mirror` makes the destination match the source exactly — every ref created, updated or DELETED to match. That last word is why it must never be pointed at a live repository by accident.
steps.expect: The new host holds exactly the same six refs.

verify.label: every ref reached the new host

steps.title: Verify the migration properly
steps.why: Compare ref lists and the shas they point at, not just the counts. A migration is only done when both sides resolve every ref to the same object.
commands: sh -c 'diff ../src-refs.txt ../dst-refs.txt && echo "IDENTICAL: every ref points at the same object"'
steps.expect: An empty diff — the two repositories are ref-for-ref identical.

verify.label: source and destination resolve every ref to the same object
verify.hint: compare for-each-ref output on both sides

steps.title: Keep the mirror updated as a backup
steps.why: A mirror clone configured with `remote.origin.fetch = +refs/*:refs/*` and `--mirror=fetch` can be refreshed with a plain `git fetch`. That one command in a cron job is a complete off-site backup.

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Add alerts after the migration"

commands: sh -c 'cd ../mirror.git && git fetch -q --prune && git for-each-ref | wc -l'
steps.expect: The mirror picks up the new commit and the new tag with one fetch.

verify.label: a plain fetch refreshed the backup mirror
verify.hint: a --mirror clone fetches every ref by default

steps.title: Prove the backup is restorable
steps.why: A backup nobody has restored is a hope, not a backup. Clone from the mirror and check the branch count, tags and notes all survive the round trip.

verify.label: the restored copy has every ref, including the new tag

steps.title: Repoint your working clone and finish
steps.why: The migration ends when developers point at the new host. It is one config change each — the object database does not care which server it came from.

verify.label: your clone now points at the new host
the migration moved every ref, not just the default branch
the migration was verified ref-by-ref, not assumed
the backup mirror stays current with a plain fetch
the backup was actually restored and checked
the working clone was repointed at the new host

pitfalls: `git push --mirror` DELETES refs on the destination that the source does not have. Never point it at a repository that has anything the source lacks.
A normal clone does not bring notes, and brings only the tags reachable from what it fetched. For a migration, always mirror.
`--mirror` clones are bare and have no working tree. Do not try to develop in one; clone from it instead.
Verify with `for-each-ref` output on both sides, not by counting branches in a web UI. Hidden refs — notes, replace, pull-request refs — are exactly what gets lost.
Some forges keep pull-request refs under `refs/pull/*`. A mirror copies them, which is usually what you want for an archive and usually not what you want on the new host.
cheatsheet: a bare copy of the entire ref namespace
make the destination match exactly — including deletions
the list to diff when verifying
refresh a mirror clone; that is your backup job
repoint a working clone after migration
